L'impossible quête pour une alternative souveraine et privée à Google Maps

2026-07-11 Corentin Béchade (Les Numériques) Google Maps, sovereign alternative, privacy, open-source mapping, Crowdsourcing, Apple Plans, Cartes.gouv, OSM, market dominance, network effects
Read the source article

Quick summary

After four years trying to replace Google Maps with sovereign and privacy-respecting alternatives, a journalist concludes that the problem is more political than technical — user data and network effects lock everyone into Google's mapping monopoly.

Key takeaways

  • Google Maps has effectively become a social network where every review, photo, and comment reinforces its dominance, creating a vicious circle of user lock-in
  • 73% of surveyed French users prefer a public-institution map over a tech giant's, and 56% are bothered by mapping apps recording their movements (Cartes.gouv survey)
  • Even Apple with its hundreds of billions has failed to make Plans a serious competitor to Google Maps
  • The problem is political rather than technical: viable alternatives exist (OSM-based apps, Cartes.gouv, HERE WeGo) but lack the crowdsourced data depth that makes Maps indispensable
  • The article is the first installment of a series exploring how to escape Google's ecosystem, following the author's four-year personal experiment
